chunks: Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ali ibn Salim from Yahya ibn Muhammad said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'O you who have believed, when death approaches one of you, [in the case of] bequest, two just witnesses from among you or two others from outside [the believers].'

He said: 'The two from among you are two Muslims, and the two from outside [the believers] are from the People of the Book - and if you do not find People of the Book, then from the Magians, because the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) established for the Magians the same ruling as the People of the Book regarding the jizya.'
He said: 'And that is if he dies in a foreign land and does not find two Muslims, then two men from the People of the Book are made to testify.'

'After the prayer, so they swear by Allah if you doubt, that we will not buy it for a price, even if he were a relative, and we will not conceal the testimony of Allah; indeed, we would then be of the sinners.'

He said: 'And that is if the heir of the deceased doubts their testimony, and if he finds that they testified falsely, he is not allowed to invalidate their testimony until two other witnesses come and take the place of the first two witnesses.'
'So they swear by Allah that our testimony is more worthy than their testimony, and we did not transgress; indeed, we would then be of the wrongdoers.'
So when he does that, the testimony of the first two is invalidated and the testimony of the latter two is accepted.
Allah, Exalted and Mighty, says: 'That is nearer that they bring the testimony in its true form or they fear that oaths will be returned after their oaths.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for witnesses of a will if no Muslims are available?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, highlighting the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in applying the principle of 'Sunnah of the People of the Book' to Magians for wills in foreign lands. The text elaborates on the procedural nuance where, if the heir doubts the testimony, two new witnesses can be brought to swear their testimony is superior, thereby nullifying the first pair's testimony to ensure accuracy.
